source.title: TFANet: a temporal fusion attention neural network for motor imagery decoding
source.authors: Chao Zhang; Ya Liu; Xiao-Pei Wu

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling that affects this assessment.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies motor-imagery EEG decoding and reports test accuracy and a training-loss trend. It does not test whether the named network training recipes reach zero or near-zero training classification error, nor does it test the other claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports held-out test accuracy, module ablations, and a qualitative training-loss trend. It does not report training classification error, so those accuracy results are not rows for the claim versions. One row records the training-loss trend as a related finding outside the versions.
record.test_reason: TFANet uses batch normalization and residual connections, citing Santurkar et al. and He et al., but evaluates its EEG decoding method rather than their optimization claims. It reports held-out accuracy and a qualitative training-loss decline, without training classification error or controlled comparisons of depth, initialization, normalization, width, or learning-rate stability.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that TFANet offers competitive MI-EEG decoding with a useful balance of performance, computational efficiency, and practicality, and potential for real-time BCI applications and clinical translation.
record.recipe_differences: Trains an EEG motor-imagery decoder with Adam and cross-entropy on BCIC-IV-2a and BCIC-IV-2b; the paper does not evaluate the claim’s training-classification-error outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: TFANet's training loss decreases and stabilizes after approximately 100 iterations on BCIC-IV-2a, with no numerical final loss or training classification error reported in the supplied text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: TFANet exhibits a declining and stabilizing training-loss trajectory on BCIC-IV-2a under its reported Adam training recipe.

record.problems: The reported training-loss trend is qualitative in the text and has no stated uncertainty. The methods section and conclusion report different learning rates (0.0005 and 0.0001, respectively). Training classification error is not reported.
record.rows_left_out: No other results meet the claim’s training-classification-error requirement. The reported held-out accuracy comparisons, ablations, perturbation analyses, and attention-head comparisons concern EEG decoding performance rather than training classification error.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, corrupted labels, and dependence on model size or training recipe.
Spurious minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and their reduction through extra student width.
Training-error degradation with depth, prevention by identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization and normalization exceptions.
Effects of initialization on signal propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Recovery or divergence relative to the initial stability limit and subsequent curvature or sharpness dynamics.
Training-speed and learning-rate-tolerance comparisons with and without batch normalization, including Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Using normalization and residual connections does not test their optimization benefits. Module ablations report held-out decoding accuracy, not depth-related training degradation. Methods specify learning rate 0.0005; the conclusion specifies 0.0001. Figure 8's plotted values are unavailable in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, including with corrupted or random labels, and the effects of model size, early stopping, and regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth, identity shortcuts, plain networks, and the specified initialization or normalization conditions.
Initialization effects on training speed or trainable depth.
Training behavior at or above a learning-rate stability limit and sharpness dynamics.
Batch normalization effects on training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and normalization-free residual training.

rows.subject: TFANet
rows.operation_detail: Training-loss trend on BCIC-IV-2a; no numerical loss values reported in the text.
rows.value: Training loss decreased significantly and stabilized after ∼100 iterations.
rows.note: The text reports training loss, not training classification error; the figure is described qualitatively. The conclusion separately states a learning rate of 0.0001, while the methods section states 0.0005.
rows.check: The qualitative loss decline is accurately recorded, but neither its final magnitude nor training classification error is supplied. It cannot establish any claim version. Section 3.7 calls the stabilization point approximately 100 iterations, whereas Figure 8 describes epochs; preserve this reporting ambiguity.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
